synopsis: The EU Machinery Regulation applies from 20 January 2027; Annex I Part A covers self-evolving machine-learning safety components and machinery embedding them, and every Part A conformity route involves a notified body [f12407, f15106]. Whether a trained perception model frozen before delivery qualifies as “self-evolving” remained disputed and unsettled in 2026, so the booklet recommends planning for notified-body involvement for EU products using machine learning in safety functions unless legal advice concludes otherwise [f15107, f2643]. No published commitment or precedent accepting off-road simulation evidence was found, and the competence needed to assess a simulation-based collision-mitigation argument was not identified [f258, f7417, f8243]. Notified-body lead times were also not found; the warning that assessment alone could exceed the four-month validation window is therefore a planning risk, not a documented duration [f259, f364]. The booklet recommends early notified-body and counsel consultation on both legal scope and simulation acceptance, escalating if physical confirmation is required but unscheduled [f10960, f10962]. Its timing advice is in tension: contact is described as realistic by mid-2027 for a team starting in October 2026, while absence of pre-consultation by early 2027 is already treated as a warning sign of regulatory rejection [f855, f11056].
